image.alt: Harsh Yadav, founding engineer at Libra AI

chapters.title: The first version
chapters.note: Joined as an intern, founding engineer from July
lines: Built most of the web app's first version: chat, mentions, file previews, onboarding.
Rebuilt search so keyword and vector results run together and merge.
Built the BI assistant: chat over a team's data, with agents that write and fix SQL.
Let people undo the agent's edits in Notion, Linear and Google Sheets.
Built sub-agents that split a big request and work the parts in parallel.

chapters.title: The agent loop
lines: Wrote the agent loop that became Libra's default chat.
Built approvals, so the agent asks before it changes anything in a team's connected apps.
Made chat answers keep streaming after you reload the page.
Built slide generation and editing, with PowerPoint and PDF export.
Cut the agent's token use with shorter tool results, summaries and prompt caching.

chapters.title: The desktop app
lines: Started the macOS desktop app and ran its releases.
Built a Spotlight-style assistant and push-to-talk dictation for the Mac app.
Made the Mac app record both sides of a meeting: your mic and the call's audio.

chapters.title: Custom agents
lines: Built custom agents: describe one in chat, run it on a schedule or event, or group agents into a team.
Rebuilt the agent's tools for GitHub, Slack, Linear, Notion, Asana and Calendar.
Made approvals durable: the agent pauses for a yes and picks up when it comes.

chapters.title: Agent core
lines: Rewrote the agent as one core that every chat runs on, whatever the model.
Let the agent use a browser and real Mac apps from the desktop app.
Wrote stress evals: 115 tasks against a simulated 3,500-person company, then fixed what broke.

chapters.title: Libra anywhere
lines: Rebuilt self-hosting so a team can run Libra on its own server, with signed updates.
Built Libra's native iOS app in SwiftUI: chat, tasks and meeting recording.
Built Libra's MCP server, so Claude and ChatGPT can search a team's Libra.
Gave custom agents spend limits and approvals, so a run stops or asks before writing.
